summary.intent: Add scheduled mutation-testing and fuzzing CI jobs to the callisto repo, modeled on the existing scheduled advisories workflow, following the already-opened PR #373.
summary.outcome: Verified locally that cargo-fuzz and cargo-mutants invocations work, wrote a sharded scheduled workflow (callisto-quality.yml), linted it with zizmor, ran workflow contracts, added a CONTRIBUTING.md note, and shipped a PR for it.

repo: Scheduled workflows in callisto follow the existing advisories workflow pattern, with pinned actions (including a pinned upload-artifact) verified by pin checks.
Workflow contract tests exist and were run against the new workflow; zizmor is used to lint workflows.
Mutant counts: callisto-model has 1,112 mutants and callisto-manifests has 404, too many for a single CI job.
Mutation testing runs at about 2.7 s per mutant; a small 11-mutant shard surfaced 4 missed mutants, indicating test gaps.
Fuzz targets run locally with cargo-fuzz on a nightly toolchain: about 92k and 430k executions in 30 s for two targets, with no crashes.
Fuzz and mutants runs can leave stray output files, so the worktree was checked for them before shipping.
workflow: Prove tool invocations locally (fuzz for 30 s, small mutants shard with timing) before encoding them in CI.
Use measured per-mutant timing to pick the shard count (6 shards, about 15 min each) so jobs fit CI limits.
Lint new workflows with zizmor and run the contract tests before opening the PR.
Check for stray artifacts after fuzz and mutation runs.

friction: Mutation and fuzz runs risk leaving stray output files in the worktree, requiring an explicit cleanliness check.
Several Bash calls were split or repeated (counting mutants, shard timing, contract checks), suggesting combined commands were awkward or failed.
open_items: The 4 missed mutants found in the small shard indicate test coverage gaps that were not addressed in this session.
Full-scale scheduled runs of the 6 mutation shards and the fuzz job have not yet been observed in CI, so timing and timeout assumptions are unvalidated.
The 6-shard split is estimated from 2.7 s per mutant and may need tuning once real CI runs complete.
